thread:
oliver: Quick notehit a parity gotcha: Go SDK POSTs /v1/alerts with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 and the server treats body as raw string, expecting JSON with fields. curl example works. sample-app alert creation failed.

kyle: can you paste repro?

oliver: curl
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/alerts \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"name":"disk","threshold":90}'
```
works. Go SDK call:
```go
client.Alerts.Create(ctx, AlertsCreateParams{Name:"disk", Threshold:90})
```
server logs show content-type text/plain and body "Name=disk&Threshold=90"

mara: that's urlencoded form encoding. generator probably set form serialization by mistake for structs with simple fields. we used to default to JSON.

kyle: yep found it: recent codegen tweak maps small flat structs to application/x-www-form-urlencoded for historical reasons. this is wrong for REST endpoints that expect JSON. impacts onboarding because sample-app uses Alerts.Create a lot.

oliver: also noticed the Go SDK sets Content-Type header explicitly, so proxies don't rewrite it.

kyle: plan: 1) hotfix generator to prefer application/json unless spec has formData, 2) add a parity smoke that compares curl vs SDK content-type and body shape for create endpoints, 3) patch SDK to fall back to JSON serialization if server returns 415. I'll open INF-3888.

devx-bot: Created issue INF-3888: "Go SDK form-encodes simple structs -> content-type/body mismatch vs API" assigned to kyle.

kyle: PR 922 opened with generator fix + unit test. Also adding a runtime fallback to retry with JSON if server rejects form-encoded payload. Cutting 0.9.9-hotfix now.

mara: please add a short note in the upgrading guide: "SDK serialization changed back to JSON; if you relied on form-encoding, explicitly set the header/serializer."

kyle: released 0.9.9-hotfix, pinned sample-app, onboarding green. Closing INF-3888 after verification.

oliver: confirmed staging and production for new customer. thanks! :tada:
